subject: CartScale pipeline congestion - cross-functional plan & external note
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] CartScale p99 jump + throughput drop - immediate triage

Team,

We started seeing a sustained p99 latency jump and a concurrent throughput drop impacting CartScale's production cluster (cartscale-prod-us-west-2) starting ~08:45 PDT. Quick snapshot:
- p50 ~ stable (~120ms)
- p95 ~ +40% (from baseline)
- p99 ~ ~3x (baseline 900ms -> ~2.7s)
- Aggregate QPS down ~40% from usual; queue depth for tokenized generation up ~120%
- Error rate remains low (2xx majority) but client timeouts are up and customers are seeing slow responses in checkout flows.

This is customer-impacting; Amit/Shah on the account is on standby. Grace: can you kick off the SRE triage? Karthik/Kimberly: product-level questions below — we may need a short-term routing exception or model fallback while SRE stabilizes.

Immediate asks:
1) SRE triage - root cause hypothesis and recommended mitigation (Grace)
2) Product decision on temporary model downgrade (quality vs latency) and whether to allow routing to medium-quantized variant (Kimberly)
3) CS/customer note draft — we need an ETA to provide to CartScale and an ask list for credits/SLAs (Marissa)

I will coordinate comms once we have the mitigation path. Attaching incident metrics snapshot (internal only).

Thanks,
Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: incident-metrics-0800.png (image), perf-heap-sample.txt
From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-20T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] CartScale p99 jump + throughput drop - immediate triage

Rafael — initial triage results below. I'm still digging but wanted to share the high-confidence observations so we can move on mitigations in parallel.

What I've seen so far:
- Kernel/kernel-scheduler stalls on the serving hosts coincident with a rise in KV cache misses for the cart-preload prefix (miss rate +210%).
- Batch formation times increased due to token fanout variance for several large requests (long-tail prompts from CartScale). Continuous batching is widening batch windows; effective per-token latency increases.
- No obvious memory pressure or OOMs; CPU on the infer hosts is within expected range but a subset of GPUs show elevated context-switch gaps.

Immediate mitigations I can run (low risk):
A) Enable aggressive prefix caching/warmup for CartScale (1-2m to take effect) — should cut KV miss rate and reduce p99.
B) Force-fallback: route 20% of traffic to redwood-gen-medium (faster per-token but slightly lower quality) as a stop-gap.
C) Increase per-instance concurrency cap by +10% for affected pool to lower queue depth (briefly increases QPS on infra).

I'll prepare short logs and a diagnostics bundle (msrc-diagnostics-0520.txt) and a raw heap profile (heap-profile-raw.pb). If product approves B we should coordinate the rollout window and customer notice.

Action items (proposed owners):
- Grace: run A now, assemble diagnostics bundle (ETA 30m)
- Rafael: coordinate customer note + approval to route (owner: Rafael/Marissa)
- Kimberly/Karthik: confirm whether 20% medium fallback acceptable for the account and if we want an SLO exception for the window

I'll update in 30.

—Grace
SRE

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] CartScale p99 jump + throughput drop - immediate triage

Thanks Grace — good triage. A few product/roadmap notes before we decide on fallback routing: 

1) Tradeoffs: redwood-gen-medium reduces median-output quality in long-context generation by ~5-8% on our eval sets for CartScale prompts; however it usually drops p99 latency by ~600-900ms. For a checkout flow, latency wins.
2) If we route 20% to medium now, what's the gating to revert? Test window suggestion: 2 hours + monitoring for regression on quality metrics.
3) Roadmap acceleration ask: the cache warmup optimization (RED-5821) is slated for Q3 — can we triage a quick patch to the cache prefetch logic to reduce cold-miss amplification? If yes, what's the rough ETA for a hotfix?

For customer messaging: propose we offer an operational update with 3 items: what happened (brief), what we're doing now (A/B fallback + warmup), and expected timeline (ETA 2 hours for mitigation visible, full stabilization 24-48h). Marissa, can you draft a note we can share with Amit? Rafael, I'll need a quick signoff on the fallback decision.

Kimberly
PM, Model Serving

We are seeing user-visible slowdowns on checkout and a 6% drop in conversions since 08:50 PDT. This is high-severity for us; our ops team is on the line. Can you confirm an ETA for mitigation? We need a specific timeline for our execs. Also flagging that any routing to a lower-quality model will need prior acknowledgement by our product team; we're open to temporary fallbacks if they are timeboxed.

Amit Shah

CartScale Inc.

Subject: RE: CartScale performance - mitigation plan (draft customer note)

Amit — thanks for the call a few minutes ago. High-level plan and ETA below; short customer note attached (customer-brief-v1.docx).

What happened (short):
We observed an unusual increase in KV cache misses for CartScale server pools that caused batch formation times to widen. That in turn elevated p99 latency and reduced effective throughput. No data loss.

Immediate steps we are taking (next 120 minutes):
- Enabling aggressive prefix cache warmup for CartScale (Grace) — expected visible improvement in ~10-30 minutes.
- Rolling a controlled 20% fallback to redwood-gen-medium for long-context generation requests (if you approve) to reduce client-observed p99 latency while cache warmup proceeds.
- Monitoring dashboards and quality checks for the fallback cohort; full rollback if we see >2% degradation in key quality signals.

ETA: expect measurable latency improvement within 30 minutes of the cache warmup; full stabilization targeted within 24 hours.

Customer ask/credits: Marissa will follow up on any SLA/credit needs; we will treat this as a priority for review.

Next steps / how we will keep you updated:
- 11:15: Grace posts diagnostics bundle and short runbook on the shared Drive link.
- 11:30: We kick the 20% fallback (if you OK) and monitor for 1 hour, then scale back if quality impact exceeds the threshold.
- 14:00: Written follow-up with final telemetry and proposed make-good (if applicable).

If you approve the fallback, reply-all with a one-line confirmation. I will send an updated note to your broader ops/executive list.

Apologies for the impact — we are treating this with the highest priority.

—Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Following up with the diagnostics bundle and a short synthesis after the mitigations.

Timeline / outcomes:
- 09:35 PDT (May 20): Enabled prefix cache warmup — observed KV miss rate drop ~65% in affected pools within 12 minutes.
- 11:30 PDT: Deployed 20% fallback to redwood-gen-medium for long-context requests as approved; p99 for customer cohort dropped ~1.1s on average, queue depth normalized.
- 13:45 PDT: Observed a secondary micro-regression associated with a nightly job from an internal data sync that increased token fanout variance; reverted the job and rates stabilized.

Files attached to this message (internal):
- msrc-diagnostics-0520.txt (logs + timeline)
- heap-profile-raw.pb (raw profile; large)

Recommended next steps (product + infra):
1) Schedule a focused hotfix for cache prefetch guard (RED-5821) — target patch in 2 weeks, engineering effort estimate: 3 engineer-weeks. Kimberly: can you prioritize this?
2) Expand continuous-batching observation windows to detect long-tail prompts earlier (SRE/infra).
3) Customer communication: Rafael/Marissa to finalize and send the short note with the updated timeline and the offer to discuss SLA accommodation.

I'll hand off the logs to the incident review. If you want, I'm available to join the customer call — otherwise Rafael, please send the updated customer-facing email.

—Grace
SRE
